Guidance & outlook: As per our reading, cement demand in South, West, and East regions grew approximately 6% Y -o-Y in quarter one FY27.
Central capex grew by 24% Y -o-Y, and data indicates that 28% of the FY27 capex budget has already been uti lized in quarter one.
Now, the target laid out during the second quarter last year was to achieve 49% by 4Q FY26 and 63% by FY27.
Growth & demand: The North region, where we started sal es in this quarter, saw substantially higher demand growth of approximately 11% Y -o-Y.
Firstly, on volumes, our total sales volume in quarter 1 FY27 increased by 15% Y -o-Y to 3.81 million tons.
GGBS volume growth was relatively muted at 2.6% Y-o-Y.
Margins & costs: The market reception has been very positive so far, with a n average utilization level of 55% in quarter one.

Despite improvement in realizations, EBITDA declined mainly due to cost pressures in fuel and packing, plus the substantial marketing investment of about INR33 crores made in North region during quarter one.

Rajesh Ravi: Okay, so fair to ass ume at 55% -60% utilization, you have turned or you will be turning EBITDA break even, and thereafter profitability will further kick in with the commissioning of the WHR, OLBC, and more of low-cost fuel purchase, lignite and all.
Capex & expansion: The additional 1 million ton grinding capacity in Nagaur is also on track and is e xpected to be commissioned by end of Q2.
We added 56 megawatt of wind capacity in Q1 at Dolvi and Vijayanagar, and this took our RE share to 30% in Q1.

Other expenses have also increased by 4.5% quarter -on-quarter in absolute terms, and this is largely related to the heavy marketing investment in the North region and higher packing cost during the quarter.
Balance sheet & cash: In terms of balance sheet, net debt was INR3,856 crores at the end of June.
Average cost of debt for the quarter was stable quarter -on- quarter at 7.63%.
Narinder Singh: Net debt to EBITDA, see, the internal guidance for us from the board is to keep it below 3.0x.
Risks & challenges: FY27 has started off on a strong note for the company despite the ongoing uncertainty around the West Asia crisis and the impact of state elections held early in the quarter.
Finally, on the macro front, we continu e to monitor the external environment, which remains volatile.
Now, what we've seen is in the East and the Wes t, we've done significantly better than the than the industry, and in the South is where we had a bit of a headwind.

guidance.t: And lastly on the capex number, Q1 you have done INR337 crores and for full year you're guiding INR2,300 crores.

Guidance & outlook: At Nagaur, work has substantially advanced on the additional 1 million ton grinding and waste heat recovery system and the commissioning is expected in the next few months.
The estimated investment for this project is INR430 crores, and this unit is expected to commission by quarter 4 of FY28.
JSW Cement Limited May 21, 2026 As far as the guidance for FY27 and FY28 are concerned, we intend to spend about INR2,300 crores in FY27 and about INR2,200 crores in FY28.
Growth & demand: On volumes, our total sales volume in quarter 4 FY '26 increased b y 7% Y-o-Y to 3.99 million tons.
On a product level, cement volume sold was 2.35 million tons, increased by 12% Y-o-Y.
And the cement volumes grew 12% in the same space, resulting, of course, in increasing market share in the geography that we operate.
Margins & costs: On product ASP, cement realizations for quarter 4 FY '26 was at INR4,673 per ton, increase of 4.8% quarter-on-quarter with increases across all regions that we operate in.
GGBS realization for quarter 4 FY '26 was at INR 3,682 per ton, slight improvement on quarter-on-quarter basis.
JSW Cement Limited May 21, 2026 Our operating EBITDA margin was 19.3% in Q4 ' 26, which is a jump of 460 bps versus the same quarter last year.
Capex & expansion: Very pleased to highlight that our integrated plant at Nagaur in Rajasthan comprising of 3.3 million ton of clinker and 2.5 million tons of grinding capacity s tarted commercial operations in March 2026.
As you will have seen in our investor presentation, the Board has approved an additional 2.5 MTPA cement grinding capacity at Nagaur, taking the total grinding capacity at Nagaur to 6 MTPA.
The remaining capacity expansion plan remains on track and will take the company t o a grinding capacity of 46 MTPA with a clinker of 13.04 MTPA.
Balance sheet & cash: Based on this adjusted profit after tax for the year, the Board has recommended a dividend of INR0.50 per equity share of face value of INR10 each, and this is subject to the approval by the shareholders at the AGM.
JSW Cement Limited May 21, 2026 In terms of balance sheet, the net debt was INR3,635 crores as on 31st of March.
And we have, as of now, not yet leveraged on the strength of JSW Steel.
Risks & challenges: This creates a near -term uncertainty for overall economi c growth and for the demand outlook for cement industry as a whole.
The demand environment in April '26 has been relatively soft due to the inflationary pressures arising from the Middle East war situation.
To summarize, we believe these disruptions are behind us and volumes are rising from mid -May post-election and getting back on track.
